  CITY COUNCIL  Item 4J moved to Item 7A
  REGULAR MEETING AGENDA

  Tuesday, April 6, 2021 - 6:30 P.M.

  City Hall Council Chamber
  425 South Mission Drive
  San Gabriel, California 91776

  Teleconference into the meeting.

Pursuant to State and County Directives, San Gabriel City Hall is closed to the public and physical access
to the meeting has been suspended. To provide members of the public access to the meeting and an
opportunity to comment on items on and off the Agenda, the following opportunities have been
established:

Public Comments

Please email all public comments to cityclerk@sgch.org and include the following on the subject line of
your email: the section (Public Comment, Consent, Public Hearing, Continued Business, New Business) and
Item Number you are commenting on. The Clerk will read public comments into the record for up to the
three-minute limit. Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 6, 2021
   C. APPOINTMENTS TO INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES – COUNCIL
  LIAISONS

  The Mayor is responsible for appointing members of the City Council to serve
  on various local and regional committees and organization boards, as well as
  liaisons for City initiatives. In addition, it is necessary for the Council to take
  formal action to designate the new Mayor to serve as the Delegate to the Los
  Angeles County Sanitation District Board and Los Angeles County City
  Selection Committee.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-14
  confirming the Mayor’s appointments of Council Members to serve as
  delegates, alternates and liaisons to outside agencies and Committees.

  D. AWARD OF CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT IN THE AMOUNT OF $136,036
  FOR THE INTERSECTION SAFETY IMPROVEMENTS AT SAN GABRIEL
  BOULEVARD AND ROSES ROAD HSIP8 PROJECT, CONTRACT NO. 20-10

  California Professional Engineering, Incorporated (Contractor) is the lowest
  responsive bidder for the construction contract, Intersection Safety
  Improvements at San Gabriel Boulevard and Roses Road HSIP8 Project, in the
  amount of $136,036. This project will install crosswalk visibility enhancements,
  overhead pedestrian flashing beacons, curb ramps, and pedestrian crossing
  ahead signage.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve plans and specifications for the Intersection Safety
  Improvements at San Gabriel Boulevard and Roses Road HSIP8 Project,
  Contract No. 20-10;
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute contract documents with California
  Professional Engineering, Incorporated for total bid amount in the amount
  of $136,036; and
  3. Approve a Purchase Order in the amount of $149,640 which includes a
  10% construction contingency.

  3
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 6, 2021
   E. AWARD PROFESSIONAL SERVICE AGREEMENT TO BALFOUR BEATTY
  INFRASTRUCTURE, INCORPORATED FOR TRENCH MAINTENANCE
  SERVICES

  The City of San Gabriel is responsible for the maintenance of the 1.4-mile
  section of the Union Pacific Railroad track in a trench through the City with
  bridges constructed at Ramona Street, Mission Road, Del Mar Avenue and
  San Gabriel Boulevard, allowing vehicles and pedestrians to pass over the
  tracks. The City is responsible for scheduled monitoring, inspections and
  maintenance of structures, drainage systems, lighting, fencing, graffiti and
  weed abatement, ingress and egress facilities and all other non-rail elements
  of the trench.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute a two (2) year Professional Services
  Agreement with Balfour Beatty Infrastructure, Incorporated; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or representative to extend the term for up to
  three (3) additional years in one-year increments.

  F. AWARD PROFESSIONAL SERVICE AGREEMENT TO R.F. DICKSON
  COMPANY, INCORPORATED FOR CITYWIDE STREET SWEEPING
  SERVICES

  The City has approximately 196 curb-miles, which must be regularly swept to
  comply with State regulations. The street sweeping contract with Athens
  Services has expired and they have been continuing their services to the City
  on a month-to-month basis. After evaluating the five received proposals,
  conducting reference checks and considering one bid protest, staff, in
  conjunction with legal counsel, determined that the proposal submitted by
  R.F. Dickson Company, Incorporated substantially conformed with the RFP
  requirements and is the lowest responsive bid. The City Council is requested
  to award a new seven-year Professional Services Agreement to R.F. Dickson
  Company, Incorporated for citywide street sweeping services in an amount
  not to exceed $166,000 annually plus CPI adjustments.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  4
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 6, 2021
   1. Authorize the City Manager to execute a seven-year Professional Services
  Agreement with R.F. Dickson Company, Incorporated to begin on May 1,
  2021 and end on April 30, 2028.
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his/her representative to extend the term
  for up to three additional years in one-year increments.
  3. Authorize the issuance of a Purchase Order to R.F. Dickson Company,
  Incorporated in the amount not to exceed $28,000 for services provided
  from May 1, 2021 through the end of the current fiscal year from the Gas
  Tax funds (Contract Services – Street Sweeping) account 136-800-02-22-
  055 and Measure W funds account 138-800-03-22-000.

  G. RENEWAL OF A GENERAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH THE COUNTY OF
  LOS ANGELES FOR “AS-NEEDED” SERVICES

  The County General Services Agreement (GSA) is an umbrella agreement that
  enables the County to provide services to cities on a requested “as-needed”
  time-limited basis. San Gabriel currently obtains as-needed limited County
  Services through the GSA such as traffic signal trouble-shooting, traffic
  striping/markings, storm water catch basin cleaning and a variety of public
  works activities. On July 1, 2016, San Gabriel renewed the General Services
  Agreement with Los Angeles County for a term of five years. That renewal will
  expire on June 30, 2021.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the renewal of the General
  Services Agreement with the County of Los Angeles and authorize the Mayor
  to execute the Agreement.

  H. AMENDED AND RESTATED JOINT-USE AGREEMENT WITH SAN GABRIEL
  UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT

  Since 1998, Gabrielino High School has used Smith Park Pool for their swim
  team practices and meets. Since that time, San Gabriel Unified School District
  (District) has entered into an annual agreement with the City of San Gabriel
  for use of the City’s pool. As part of a long-standing arrangement, the District
  has paid the City a percentage of the utility costs, as well as the hourly
  lifeguard rate, for use of the pool. In April 2017, the City entered into the
  Facilities Joint-Use Agreement with the District. In order to include the pool
  usage as part of the joint-use arrangement with the District, staff is now
  proposing an Amended and Restated Facilities Joint-Use Agreement. The
  Amended Agreement includes Exhibit G with the specific details for Smith

  5
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 6, 2021
   Park Pool. Though an Amended Joint-Use Agreement was reviewed by the
  City Council in May 2019, it was not approved by the District at that time. The
  Agreement has now been approved by the District and, as such, is once again
  being brought to the City Council for review and approval.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the proposed
  Amended and Restated Facilities Joint-Use Agreement and authorize the City
  Manager and Mayor to execute the agreement.

  I. 2020 GENERAL PLAN IMPLEMENTATION ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT:
  JANUARY 2020 – DECEMBER 2020

  As required by Government Code Section 65400(a)(2), the Planning Division
  is required to provide an annual report each April to the City Council, and the
  State Governor’s Office of Planning and Research (OPR) regarding the status
  of the General Plan and its implementation progress. The Planning
  Commission reviewed the attached information at their March 8, 2021
  meeting, affirmed the information in the report and recommended it be
  forwarded to the City Council.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the information
  contained in the staff report and direct staff to submit the report to the Office
  of Planning and Research (OPR) and State Department of Housing and
  Community Development (HCD).

  5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 21-15 CONDEMNING RACISM, XENOPHOBIA, AND
  INTOLERANCE AGAINST ASIAN AMERICANS AND PACIFIC ISLANDERS

  Since the outbreak of the Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic,
  nationwide and in California, there has been a rise in reported hate incidents

  6
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – April 6, 2021
   and crimes against Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders (AAPIs). Resolution
  No. 21-15 condemns anti-Asian racism and affirms the City’s commitment to
  equity and justice for all members of the community.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-15
  Condemning Racism, Xenophobia, and Intolerance Against Asian Americans
  and Pacific Islanders.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members
  to report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, April 20, 2021, at

MINUTES OF APRIL 6, 2021
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Liao called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:48 P.M.
  on Tuesday, April 6, 2021, with all Council Members and staff participating by
  teleconference.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  DRAFT AUDIT BY BUREAU OF STATE AUDITS (Government Code Section 54956.75)

  Assistant City Attorney Pilchen announced that in the preceding special meeting, no
  reportable final action was taken on the closed session item.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Liao.

I  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  John R. Harrington, Denise Menchaca, Jason Pu, Vice
  Mayor Tony Ding, and Mayor Chin Ho Liao.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City
  Manager/Community Development Director Armine
  Chaparyan, Assistant City Attorney Lloyd Pilchen,
  Community  Services/Interim  Mission  Playhouse
  Director Rebecca Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris,
  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City
  Engineer Greg de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace,
  Human Resources/Risk Management Director Edward
  Macias, Finance Director William Kaholokula, and
  Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and

I  submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Liao announced that the Agenda Order was approved.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. RECOGNITION OF OUTGOING MAYOR, AND INCOMING MAYOR AND VICE
  MAYOR

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 6  Apri l 6, 2021
   1. Recognition of Outgoing Mayor Menchaca

  Chief City Clerk Clark announced that outgoing Mayor Menchaca had been
  presented with a gavel plaque from the City to commemorate her term as
  Mayor.

  The following presented comments recognizing outgoing Mayor Menchaca,
  incoming Mayor Liao and incoming Vice Mayor Ding: Cindy Lee, Representative

I  from Congresswoman Judy Chu 's Office; 5 t h District Supervisor Kathryn Barger;
  and Alhambra Vice Mayor Katherine Lee.

  Chief City Clerk Clark noted that Certificates of Recognition for outgoing
  Mayor Menchaca had been received from Senator Susan Rubio;
  Assemblymember Ed Chau; Supervisor Kathryn Barger; the Cities of Alhambra,
  Arcad ia, Duarte, La Puente, Monrovia, Monterey Park, San Dimas, and Temple
  City; and from the San Gabriel Unified School District. Senator Rubio also
  provided certificates for Mayor Liao and Vice Mayor Ding .

  Mayor Liao, Vice Mayor Ding and Council Members Harrington and Pu thanked
  outgoing Mayor Menchaca for her leadership and service during her term as
  mayor.

  Outgoing Mayor Menchaca thanked her colleagues, staff, and family and
  friends; and recognized incom ing Mayor Liao and Vice Mayor Ding.

  2. New Vice Mayor's Comments

I  Vice Mayor Ding thanked his colleagues for their trust in selecting him as Vice
  Mayor; thanked those who elected him to the City Council; thanked City
  Manager Lazzaretto and staff for helping him learn in his position as a Council
  Member; thanked community organizations for their donations of Personal
  Protective Equipment (PPE) during the pandemic; and thanked his fam ily fo r
  their support.

  3. New Mayor's Comments

  Mayor Liao expressed his appreciation for being selected as Mayor; commented
  on the challenges of the pandemic; gave local vaccination site and pandem ic-
  related City assistance information; provided suggestions to improve City
  finances; expressed his wish for love and harmony in the commun ity; and
  thanked his colleagues and staff for their work during the pandemic.

  B. COVID-19 BRIEFING

  Fire Chief Wallace and Police Chief Harris made the presentation .

I  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Sean McMorris, resident, provided comments commending outgoing Mayor
  Menchaca on her year as mayor, and congratulating incoming Mayor Liao and Vice
  Mayor Ding.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  CITY COUNC IL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 6  Ap ril 6, 2021
   Chief City Clerk Clark stated that a request to pull item 4F, Award of Professional
  Service Agreement to R.F. Dickson Company, Incorporated, for Citywide Street-
  Sweeping Services, for separate consideration had been received from a Council
  Member and three members of the public. She read comments from Sandy Rosco,
  Executive Director of the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce; Alexis Salamanca,
  resident, business owner, and San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce President; and Terri
  Huerta, resident; requesting that the Request for Proposals (RFP) be withdrawn and
  the current contract with Athens Services for street-sweeping be continued as it is the
  most fiscally-prudent solution.

I  In addition, regarding Item 4C, Appointments to Intergovernmental Agencies, Chief
  City Clerk Clark explained it had come to staff's attention that according to Metro
  Service Council Bylaws, membership on the Council is not transferable or assignable.
  Therefore, the current appointee, Council Member Harrington, who is serving in the
  second year of a three-year term, will continue to serve until the conclusion of his
  term . She made a request, on behalf of staff, that Item 4C be approved with that
  change.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor Ding, to
  approve Consent Calendar Items 4A- 4B, 4D - 4E, and 4G - 41 as presented, and Item
  4C as amended .

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Items 4A - 48, 40 - 4£, and 4G - 41 as presented,
  and Item 4C as amended, by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, PU, DING, LIAO
  NOES:  NONE

I
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  Regarding Item 4F, discussion included an offer letter from Athens Services to
  continue providing street-sweeping services at their current rate, absent the new
  conditions of using five-year old or newer trucks and an 85% diversion rate; Air Quality
  Management District (AQMD) standards; diversion details; R. F. Dickson Company's
  indication that removing the two foregoing conditions would not change their
  proposal amount; pollutant levels and impacts of waste vehicles over and under five
  years old; weighing environmental impact with cost considerations; variables of vehicle
  types, ages, and maintenance levels; performance as a criteria; Athens Services waste
  vehicles are fueled by natural gas; and an 85% diversion rate is higher than required
  by law.

  A motion was made by Council Member Harrington, seconded by Council Member
  Menchaca, to continue this item indefinitely in order to go back to negotiate a contract
  with Athens Services at the terms of the letter they sent to the City.

  Discussion continued regarding getting information from the AQMD about vehicle

I  emissions; and not limiting the providers to be considered to only Athens Services, but
  rather directing staff to bring back additional information.

  Motion carried by a vote of 4- 1 as follows:

  AYES:  HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, DING, LIAO
  NOES:  PU
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 6  April 6, 2021
   A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the following:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of March 16, 2021 .
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of March 16, 2021.
  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved the March 3, 2021, March 18, 2021, and March 18, 2021 ,

I  Registers of Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. APPOINTMENTS TO INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES- COUNCIL LIAISONS

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 21-14 confirm ing the Mayor's
  appointments of Council Members to serve as delegates, alternates and liaisons to
  outside agencies and Committees, as amended for Council Member Harrington as
  the representative to the Metro Service Council.

  D. AWARD OF CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT IN THE AMOUNT OF $136,036 FOR
  THE INTERSECTION SAFETY IMPROVEMENTS AT SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD
  AND ROSES ROAD HSIP8 PROJECT, CONTRACT NO. 20-10

  The City Council :

  1. Approved plans and specifications for the Intersection Safety Improvements
  at San Gabriel Boulevard and Roses Road HSIP8 Project, Contract No. 20-
  1O;

I  2. Authorized the City Manager to execute contract documents with California
  Professional Engineering, Incorporated for total bid amount in the amount
  of $136,036; and
  3. Approved a Purchase Order in the amount of $149,640 which includes a
  10% construction contingency.

  E. AWARD PROFESSIONAL SERVICE AGREEMENT TO BALFOUR BEATTY
  INFRASTRUCTURE, INCORPORATED FOR TRENCH MAINTENANCE SERVICES

  The City Council:

  1. Authorized the City Manager to execute a two (2) year Professiona l Services
  Agreement with Balfour Beatty Infrastructure, Incorporated; and
  2. Authorized the City Manager or representative to extend the term for up to
  three (3) additional years in one -year increments.

  F. AWARD PROFESSIONAL SERVICE AGREEMENT TO R.F. DICKSON COMPANY,
  INCORPORATED FOR CITYWIDE STREET SWEEPING SERVICES

I  The City Council gave direction for staff to negotiate with Athens Services on a
  contract per the terms of their letter to the City as detailed above.
  G. RENEWAL OF A GENERAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH THE COUNTY OF LOS
  ANGELES FOR "AS-NEEDED" SERVICES

  The City Council approved the renewal of the General Services Agreement with the
  County of Los Angeles and authorize the Mayor to execute the Agreement.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 6  Ap ril 6, 2021
   H. AMENDED AND RESTATED JOINT-USE AGREEMENT WITH SAN GABRIEL
  UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT

  The City Council approved the proposed Amended and Restated Facilities Joint-
  Use Agreement and authorized the City Manager and Mayor to execute the
  agreement.

  I. 2020 GENERAL PLAN IMPLEMENTATION ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT:

I  JANUARY 2020- DECEMBER 2020

  The City Council received and filed the information contained in the staff report
  and directed staff to submit the report to the Office of Planning and Research (OPR)
  and State Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD).

  5. PUBLIC HEARING - None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 21-15 CONDEMNING RACISM, XENOPHOBIA, AND
  INTOLERANCE AGAINST ASIAN AMERICANS AND PACIFIC ISLANDERS

  Sean McMorris, resident, provided comments in favor of adopting the resolution .

  City Manager Lazzaretto made the staff presentation.

  Discussion included the rise in anti -Asian incidents throughout the Country; the

I  reluctance of some crime victims to report incidents; incident report statistics; the
  relevance of this item to the community; the City's new Human Equity, Access and
  Relations (HEAR) Commission and the Asian Crime Victims Working Group led by
  San Gabriel Police Captain Nakamura; encouragement for the community to report
  incidents; and appreciation for Council Member Pu 's spearheading of this item.

  A motion was made by Council Member Pu, seconded by Vice Mayor Ding, to
  adopt Resolution No. 21-15 Condemning Racism, Xenophobia, and Intolerance
  Against Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders.
  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, PU, DING, LIAO
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.

I  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto congratulated former Mayor Menchaca on a successful year
  as Mayor and thanked her for her leadership and partnership, and congratulated
  incoming Mayor Liao and Vice Mayor Ding.

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Menchaca announced the San Gabriel Mosquito and Vector Control
  District's Bite Back Virtual Tour on April 8, 2021, invited the community to participate,

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 5 of 6  April 6, 2021
   and solicited block captains for the District; announced La Casa 's Annual Gala on May
  15, 2021 ; and provided local COVID-19 vaccination site details.

  Council Member Pu commented on anti-Asian hate events; and reported on activities
  of the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Transportation
  Committee, Foothill Transit Authority, METRO, San Gabriel Valley Council of
  Governments (COG), and League of California Cities.

  Vice Mayor Ding reported on the Economic Development 10-Point Plan

I  Subcommittee and activities of the San Gabriel Hope Lions Club; and provided
  information on a possible grant opportunity for the Mission Playhouse.

  Mayor Liao reported on a webinar he attended on how to use the American Recue
  Plan.

  11. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Liao adjourned the meeting at 9:20 P.M .

  Respectfully submitted:

I
  Approved this 20th day of April, 2021 :
